1.why: verify-token and reset-password enforce token.sessionId === session.id and a matching mockAccountHash, binding each code to the requesting session, which is this mock's proxy for the user.

2.why: False: a token presented from any other session fails the token.sessionId !== session.id check, so the same code does not work for other users.

3.why: True: reset only marks the token used and updates the current session's flags; no other entries in the sessions map are invalidated, so prior sessions remain usable until their 30-minute expiry.

4.why: HTTPS is served via Bun TLS with mkcert certs, HSTS is set, and the HTTP listener 308-redirects to HTTPS, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Reset codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords are bcrypt-hashed at cost 10 — appropriate protection, though technically hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: The simulated delivery message contains only the recovery code and link and never echoes the submitted identifier or any other private user data.

7.why: All inputs pass strict allowlist validators (validIdentifier, validToken, validMfa, passwordPolicy) with length limits, and all dynamic output is rendered via textContent rather than innerHTML.

8.why: The only redirect is a hardcoded 308 to https://localhost:PORT and the verification link is same-origin; no user-controlled redirect targets exist anywhere.

9.why: There are no email templates, and the page renders all dynamic text via textContent under a strict nonce-based CSP, so no user input can appear as script or HTML.

10.why: Error pages are generic, but the raw reset token and MFA code are returned in API responses and written to the console and the on-page 'Logs' pane, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords and tokens are hashed, but the MFA secret is hardcoded in the source as MOCK_MFA_CODE = "482916".

12.why: The hardcoded, deterministic MFA code "482916" is the same for every session and functions as a default credential for the security-confirmation step.

13.why: Per-client-address throttling blocks recovery requests after 3 attempts and token/MFA verification after 5 failures within a 10-minute window, returning 429.

14.why: The recovery endpoint returns the identical generic message ('If the details match an account...') for any input, so account existence is never revealed.

15.why: Codes are 32 CSPRNG bytes (base64url), single-use, expire after 10 minutes, and are bound to the requesting session and account hash.
